question: If $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}5&1\\2&7\end{bmatrix}$ and $A-B=\begin{bmatrix}1&3\\-4&5\end{bmatrix}$, find the $(2,1)$th element of $A$.
explanation:
Step 1: The given relations are $A+B$ and $A-B$. Adding them eliminates $B$ because $(A+B)+(A-B)=2A$.
Step 2: Therefore, $$2A=\begin{bmatrix}5&1\\2&7\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}1&3\\-4&5\end{bmatrix}.$$
Step 3: Adding corresponding elements gives $$2A=\begin{bmatrix}6&4\\-2&12\end{bmatrix}.$$
Step 4: Dividing every element by $2$, we obtain $$A=\begin{bmatrix}3&2\\-1&6\end{bmatrix}.$$
Step 5: Hence, the element in the second row and first column is $a_{21}=-1$. Therefore, the required value is $-1$.
